text: So when deleting helps on a damaged dataset and beats random deletion, as it does under the hERG flips, the gain is noise removed.
On the labels as delivered, the control is the same cleanup driven by shuffled detector scores.
On hERG K_i, label smoothing passes this control with both detectors.
Label smoothing with the neighbor gap takes the network on the first single representation from 0.6380 to 0.5775 RMSE, while every shuffled run makes it slightly worse.
With the forest residual, label smoothing also improves the hybrid by more than any of three shuffles.
On hERG, label smoothing beats all its shuffles with gradient-boosted trees on the first single representation and on the second hybrid.
Caco-2 and LogD pass the control too, but by small amounts.
With down-weighting on the network's second single representation, one shuffle wins back more than half of the gain on each.
The hERG K_i smoothing gain on the hybrid holds on three folds.
In a second experiment, label smoothing improved the network's hybrid on each of folds 0, 1 and 2.
The second single representation got worse on fold 0 and better on the other two.
Deleting does not pass its control on the small-molecule labels as delivered.
On Caco-2, hERG K_i and LogD no deletion setting beat both no cleaning and every random deletion.
Buchwald--Hartwig is different.
Deleting the 20\% of reactions with the largest neighbor-label gap improves LightGBM on the hybrid and on the second single representation, and beats random deletion on both.
On the hybrid it scores 18.0417 RMSE in percentage points of yield, against 19.8986 for the best random deletion.
Random deletion alone also helped the first single representation, so this score moves between fits as well.
Putting activity-cliff molecules back after a cleanup can be tested on hERG K_i only.
On Caco-2, hERG and LogD more than half of the training molecules count as cliff molecules.
That leaves too few other molecules to draw a random set of the same size.
On hERG K_i, deleting the flagged molecules barely moves the network's hybrid.
Putting the cliff molecules back takes it to 0.5786 RMSE, against 0.5949 with random molecules put back.
Fold 2 agrees, and fold 1 does not.
On three antibody datasets, cleaning the labels as delivered also passes the shuffled-score control, and on those datasets it gave the largest gains (Section [REF]).
This section uses injected damage alone (Section [REF]).
The out-of-fold forest residual finds outliers, shifted labels and flipped classes well above chance on every dataset it ran on.
On Caco-2 under outlier noise its average precision is 0.3381, against a chance level of 0.0512.
Censoring is the exception.
At a clipped share of 0.25 the residual falls below chance on Buchwald--Hartwig and LogD, and is only a little above it on Caco-2.
A model fitted to clipped labels predicts values near the limit for the clipped molecules, so their residuals are small.
This is the behavior Chapter [REF] found in the models' own uncertainty, which was lowest on exactly the labels that had been clipped.
The cliff-aware gap does better than the residual when only some labels are shifted.
Under the shift in 10\%, its median neighbor setting reaches 0.2686 on Caco-2 against 0.2023 for the residual, and every one of its settings is ahead.
Under outliers only its best setting is ahead, and under censoring it trails the residual on Caco-2, hERG K_i and LogD at every setting.
So no detector is best everywhere.
A neighbor detector is better at a shift that moves a few labels a long way.
A model residual is as good or better at outliers.
The space in which the neighbors are found changes detection little (Section [REF]).
Taking the best setting in each family, the importance-weighted features were best on Buchwald--Hartwig, Caco-2, hERG K_i, LogD and SMAC colloidal stability.
On Caco-2 under outliers the four families reach average precisions close to each other, all far above chance.
The hybrid's own features were the best family on the change in binding free energy ( G) under outliers.
They were also best on SMAC colloidal stability under censoring and on Caco-2 under the shift sized by model error, but on no dataset overall.
Averaged over the detector settings instead of taking the best one, the hybrid's features come out ahead more often, so this ranking depends on how a detector's setting is chosen.
Scaling each feature by its importance before the neighbors are found raised detection under the shift in 10\%, and lowered it under censoring on every dataset.
The largest gain was on Buchwald--Hartwig, 0.4647 to 0.5123 average precision, with smaller gains on LogD and SMAC colloidal stability.
Under outliers scaling barely changed detection.
Importance is computed against the damaged labels, so under censoring it likely rewards the features that predict the clipped values, and the clipped molecules then look like their neighbors.
A Gaussian process's own predicted spread plus its residual is the one model-uncertainty detector that could be graded.
The three that predict a spread from the features alone never see a label, and the files mark them as undefined under every damage kind that can be graded.
The GP was slightly ahead of the cliff-aware gap under outliers on Caco-2 and LogD, and behind it under every shift and every hERG flip kind.
Detectors from outside cheminformatics did better than the residual where the residual is weakest.
Under censoring the nearest-neighbor Shapley value reached 0.3906 on Buchwald--Hartwig against 0.1949 for the residual, and was also ahead on SMAC colloidal stability.
Under the shift in 10\% the cleanlab score was well ahead of the residual on Buchwald--Hartwig.
The Shapley value's best number is taken over many more settings than the residual's, so these gaps lean in its favor.
Two more experiments graded the plain residual under damage sized by the model's own error.
It ranked the shifted molecules above chance on every dataset there, for example 0.20 to 0.25 against 0.106 on expression titer.
Turning such a ranking into a decision is harder.
Conformal p-values with a false-discovery-rate rule flagged no molecule at all at q = 0.05.
At q = 0.1 they flagged none when the calibration set was drawn from the noisy training labels.
Only with a clean calibration set, which a user would not have, did it flag a few dozen molecules at most in a few passes.
Acting on those flags left the held-out score where it was in almost every pass.
The break-even precision explains when acting on a detector can work (Section [REF]).
Under outliers the residual's top 5\% are mostly damaged molecules, and its precision is above the break-even on Caco-2 and hERG K_i.
Under the shift sized by model error, the residual's precision falls below the break-even.
On Caco-2 the residual's top 5\% has a precision of 0.17, and deleting them only pays off above 0.62.
On hERG K_i under the plain shift in 10\%, the precision of the top 10\% is also far below its break-even.
So a detector that ranks the damaged labels above chance can still lead to a worse model.
Acting on its flags helps only above the break-even, which depends on the damage, the action and the model.
Figure [REF] applies this test to the two learners.
Each flags the training molecules with the largest loss, and we delete every molecule that either one flags, so slightly more than the flagged share is deleted.
Under the shift in 10\% on hERG K_i, the deleted molecules have a precision of 0.23 to 0.26, against a break-even of 0.32 to 0.68.
Deleting raised the RMSE at every share, from 0.6275 to between 0.6913 and 0.7282, on 2 of the 3 noise draws because the run has not finished.
On Caco-2 under the same shift the precision was 0.14 to 0.16, against break-evens of 0.37 to 0.58, and every share again raised the RMSE.
LogD has no break-even yet.
There, under outliers, deleting at 5\% with a precision of 0.36 lowered the RMSE from 0.5874 to 0.5571, on 2 of 3 draws.

Chapter [REF] brings these results together with the rest of the thesis.
The first half of the thesis asked four questions about label noise, answered in Chapter [REF].
First, model family decided noise robustness more than the representation did.
On QM9 under Gaussian noise, model family explained 47.2\% of the variance in and the representation 8.1\%.
The representation mattered more for predictive performance.
Second, random forests were the most consistent model under noise, while LightGBM and XGBoost predicted well on clean labels and lost the most as noise rose.
Third, the type of noise mattered more than the shape of its distribution.
Systematic noise, shared within a scaffold family or clipped at an assay limit, did the most damage, so a study that injects only Gaussian noise misses it.
Fourth, mean predicted uncertainty rose with noise, but no model's uncertainty identified the corrupted labels.
Chapter [REF] then asked why published methods for learning with noisy labels did poorly in an exploratory study carried out earlier in this project.
The methods that compared molecules by a distance did worst.
Within one dataset, most features of a standard representation barely vary.
On hERG K_i, 1,815 of the 2,048 ECFP4 features take one value in at least 95\% of the molecules.
A distance sums over every feature, so these features dominate it.
The second half asked whether the representation can be adapted to the task.
First, the best set of features depends on the dataset and the downstream model, and a search can find it (Chapter [REF]).
The adaptive hybrid representation beat the best single representation on every small-molecule dataset with both downstream models.
On LogD with the SVM it went from 0.4930 to 0.4302 RMSE.
A method built for small molecules also carried over to antibodies, where the gain depended on the dataset.
On two antibody datasets the best single representation was one built for this thesis, which reads only the regions or mutations that vary.
Second, distance in a hybrid tracked the label better on all five small-molecule datasets, and predicting each label from its five nearest neighbors was more accurate (Chapter [REF]).
On hERG K_i the Spearman correlation between the distance of two molecules and the difference in their activity went from 0.0729 to 0.2625.
On antibodies and reactions distance also tracked the label better, but prediction from neighbors was worse on several datasets.
Third, noisy labels could be found and corrected (Chapter [REF]).
With a quarter of LogD's training labels clipped, censored EM took the network from 0.6354 to 0.4795 RMSE, against 0.4314 before clipping.
Cleaning guided by a detector beat random deletion or shuffled detector scores on hERG, hERG K_i, Buchwald--Hartwig and three antibody datasets.
On small molecules the hybrid stayed ahead of the single representation through every treatment.
Fourth, importance helped in building the hybrid but not in training.
The hybrid ranks features by importance within each representation.
At the same number of features it beat recursive feature elimination and random features on all but one small-molecule dataset with a result.
Using the importance scores again during training added little.
Label noise was handled, but no single method handled it on every dataset.
Which method worked depended on the prediction task, the data, the model and the type of noise.
The forest residual detector fell to chance under clipping, where acting on the known flag did best.
Subtracting scaffold-family offsets made the model worse on Caco-2's labels as delivered.
Deleting the molecules the network fits worst helped on the reactions but almost never on small molecules.
The ranking of the methods also changed between the hybrid and the single representations.
We therefore recommend modeling the noise in a dataset before choosing a method.
Data pooled from several laboratories can carry an offset per source, and an assay with a reporting limit gives clipped labels.
Both come with a flag that a correction can use.
A method that assumes noise that is not there does harm.
Simple methods were often as good as complex ones: random forests were the most consistent model, and on hERG K_i one constant lift for every clipped label beat censored EM.
The contributions on label noise are the following.
NoiseInject, an open-source Python package for benchmarking noise robustness and uncertainty in QSAR models (Section [REF]).
Noise conditions beyond Gaussian noise, including noise shared within scaffold families and labels clipped at an assay limit (Chapter [REF]).
A split of the variance in performance and in noise robustness between model family and representation (Chapter [REF]).

Published noise-handling methods adapted to QSAR data, for example censored EM with any downstream model, a random intercept per scaffold family, and the buddy check from meteorology as a detector of noisy labels (Chapter [REF]).
Three methods for which we found no earlier use (Chapter [REF]).
These are the cliff-aware gap, cleaning the labels before the hybrid search, and returning activity-cliff molecules after a cleanup.
Tests of these methods on single representations and hybrids side by side, with three controls: QM9 with no noise added, random deletion and shuffled detector scores (Chapter [REF]).
The ranking of the methods changed with the features.
The contributions on the representation are the following.

The adaptive hybrid representation, which ranks features within each representation, splits a budget of features among them, and searches the selection settings for each dataset and model (Chapter [REF]).
A newly published embedding is added to the search as one more representation.
Hybrids built for distance (Chapter [REF]), and hybrids built from data held at separate sites (Chapter [REF]).

Antibody representations built for this thesis: readouts of the complementarity-determining regions (CDRs) and of each region, mutation features, and the change in embedding from the parent antibody (Chapter [REF]).

The hybrid needs data, and most antibody datasets here hold a few hundred antibodies.
The search is costly and must be rerun when the data, the representations or the model change.
Most DNN results were computed before 8 October 2026, when the DNN began clipping each prediction to the range of its training labels.
We have not yet tested whether the best hybrid settings follow measurable properties of a dataset (Section [REF]).
The hybrid search needs only several feature matrices for the same samples and a supervised task.
Gene-expression profiles and financial time series are natural next domains, since each has many competing representations of the same samples.
Runs on DNA promoter sequences have started but are not reported here.
The noise methods need more clean controls.
QM9 offers twelve computed properties, and only the HOMO--LUMO gap was used.
In QSAR, a class label usually comes from cutting a continuous measurement at a threshold, so measurement error flips mostly the molecules near that threshold.
Flips of that kind, on more classification datasets, are the next test for the detectors.
A hybrid could also be the input to the model that scores molecules for a generative model; the code for this exists and has not been run.
A search that starts from the settings found on a similar dataset could save compute, and a deployment across real sites would test the separate-site results of Chapter [REF].
Label noise in molecular data can be handled.
Which method handles it depends on the prediction task, the data, the model and the kind of noise.
No single model, representation or noise-handling method was best on every dataset we tested.
The noise in a dataset should be understood before a method is chosen.
The features also matter.
When the noise methods failed, we followed the failure down to the distance between molecules and then to the features that distance is computed over.
The adaptive hybrid representation selects those features for each dataset and model.
On small molecules it predicted better than any single representation, gave better neighbors, and stayed ahead through every noise treatment.
A new foundation model appears every few months in molecular, protein and antibody modeling.
With the hybrid search, a researcher does not need to choose between their current representation and a new one.
They add the new embedding to the representations searched and run the search again, and the search decides whether it contributes features and which.
Chapter [REF] tested this on LogD and hERG blocking.
A choice usually made by habit becomes one measured on each task.
